diagnostic_evidence.quote: It is known that continuous maps between compact Riemannian manifolds are homotopic to HMs (cf.~\cite{EelSam64}).

issues.failure_explanation: The cited Eells–Sampson theorem guarantees a harmonic representative in each homotopy class only when the target manifold has nonpositive sectional curvature. Without this hypothesis the assertion is false (classical counterexample: degree-one maps from the flat 2-torus to the 2-sphere are homotopic to no harmonic map). The paper states it unconditionally in the abstract and introduction to motivate its analogy with fractal domains, i.e., the invoked result is used outside its hypotheses.

failure_location.quote: Every continuous map between two compact Riemannian manifolds is homotopic to a harmonic map (HM).

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Qualify the statement in the abstract and introduction (e.g., 'when the target has nonpositive sectional curvature') and cite Eells–Sampson accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The motivating manifold/fractal analogy is mathematically misstated; no formal result of the paper depends on it.
issues.title: Eells–Sampson existence claim stated without the curvature hypothesis
issues.why_classification: A local edit adding the standard hypothesis fixes it; nothing in the paper's own results changes.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: F(\tau, c_\gamma(1-0)) &=\tau f_\gamma (1-0) + (1-\tau) g_\gamma(1-0)
Thus, $F$ is a uniformly continuous function on $\mathcal{P}\times [0,1]$. Since $\mathcal{P}$ is dense in $G$ there is a unique continuous extension of $F$ to $G\times [0,1].$

issues.failure_explanation: In the converse direction the homotopy (homotopy) is not well defined: $\R/\Z$ admits no scalar multiplication by nonintegral $t$, so $tf(x)+(1-t)g(x) \mod 1$ depends on the choice of real representatives (replacing $f(x)$ by $f(x)+1$ changes the value by $t \bmod 1$). The verification then treats the $\T$-valued differences $f_\gamma(1-0)-f_\gamma(0)$ as the integer winding numbers, which is meaningful only after choosing lifts, and finally asserts that $F$ is a uniformly continuous function on $\mathcal{P}\times[0,1]$ ($\mathcal{P}$ is a family of loops, not a subset of $G$) with a continuous extension to $G\times[0,1]$ — none of which is constructed. No valid homotopy between $f$ and $g$ is produced.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the converse argument with a genuine construction, e.g., show that $f-g$ has trivial winding data and hence admits a real lift on a suitable cut/covering space and interpolate the real lifts; or invoke the standard classification $[G,S^1]\cong \check H^1(G;\Z)$ together with the fact that cell windings generate it.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed classification of homotopy classes of maps $G\to\T$ by the degree vector is not established by this proof; the interpretive statements that HMs 'represent homotopy classes' rest on it.
issues.title: Homotopy theorem proved via an ill-defined linear-interpolation homotopy
issues.why_classification: The statement is true and a correct proof is standard, but the written argument must be replaced by a different nontrivial construction rather than patched locally.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Throughout this paper, we refer to $\T$-valued solutions of \eqref{Lap} as harmonic maps (HMs) on $K$.
\Delta u(x) =0, \qquad x\in K\setminus V_0,
A function $f\in \operatorname{dom}(\cE)$ is called harmonic if it minimizes $\cE(f)$ over all continuous functions on $G$ subject to given boundary conditions on $V_0$.
$f \in L(V_m,\R)$ is called $\Gamma_m$-harmonic if it satisfies the discrete Laplace equation at every interior node of $\Gamma_m$

issues.failure_explanation: The Laplacian is defined in the paper only for real-valued functions ($L(V_m,\R)$, $\operatorname{dom}(\cE)\subset C(G,\R)$); no meaning is ever assigned to $\Delta u$ for $\T$-valued $u$, and no chartwise or liftwise interpretation is given. Thus 'HM', the central object of Theorems thm.main and thm.pcf, is defined by an equation that is meaningless for circle-valued functions. Section 6 discusses a variational interpretation but never states it as the definition of a HM, so the statements of the main theorems are ill-posed as written.

failure_location.quote: There is a unique HM $f: G\to\T$ satisfying \eqref{bc-hm} and \eqref{homotopy-c}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Adopt an explicit definition of circle-valued harmonicity (e.g., following Strichartz: the minimizer of the geodesic energy within the prescribed class, or a map that locally lifts to real harmonic functions) and restate thm.main and thm.pcf in terms of it.
issues.overall_effect: The statements of both main theorems (unique HM on SG; existence of HMs on p.c.f. sets) cannot be evaluated as stated, and all prose claims about HMs inherit the ambiguity.
issues.title: Main theorems are stated for 'harmonic maps' that are never defined for circle-valued functions
issues.why_classification: The repair is a definitional replacement compatible with the paper's constructions, but the choice is consequential and the theorems must then be proved against the chosen definition (the remaining proof gaps are tracked separately).

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \hat\cE_m(f)=\left(\frac{5}{3}\right)^m\sum_{x\sim_m y}d_\T\left(f(x), f(y)\right),
\hat\cE_m(\hat f_m^\ast)= E[\Gamma_m^0](\mathbf{f}^\ast).
we deduce that $\hat\cE_m(\hat f|_{V_m})$ forms a non-decreasing sequence for any $\hat f\in C(G,\T)$

issues.failure_explanation: Lemma lem.minimizer minimizes a quadratic energy over real-valued functions on the cut graph with prescribed boundary values. Competitors $\hat f\in\hat H$ are arbitrary continuous $\T$-valued maps on $G$: they need not lift to the cut sheet (deeper winding is unconstrained by $\hat H$), and for those that do lift, $d_\T(\hat f(x),\hat f(y))\le|\tilde f(x)-\tilde f(y)|$, so their geodesic energy is bounded above, not below, by the lifted real energy; excluding wrap-around gains requires a nontrivial argument that is not given. Moreover, (Em-hat) omits the square on $d_\T$, so the displayed identity $\hat\cE_m(\hat f^*)=E[\Gamma^0_m](\mathbf f^*)$ (a sum of squared differences) is false as written, and the monotonicity of $\hat\cE_m$ is 'deduced' from real-valued compatibility properties that do not transfer to the geodesic energy without proof. Consequently the minimality and uniqueness of the constructed map are unestablished, leaving the uniqueness part of thm.main unproven.

failure_location.quote: This combined with Lemma~\ref{lem.minimizer} implies that $\hat f^\ast$ is a unique minimizer of $\hat \cE$ in $\hat H$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define $\hat\cE_m$ with $d_\T^2$, prove monotonicity of $\hat\cE_m$ and the lower bound $\hat\cE(f)\ge E[\Gamma^0_1](f^0_1)$ (with equality analysis) for all $f\in\hat H$ with the prescribed boundary data and degree; or prove uniqueness directly by lifting any admissible HM to the covering space and using uniqueness of the real-valued Dirichlet problem there.
issues.overall_effect: The variational characterization and the uniqueness assertion of thm.main are unproven; the energy identity and monotonicity claims of Section 6 are false or unjustified as written.
issues.title: Variational argument that the constructed map is the unique HM is a non sequitur
issues.why_classification: A correct proof exists within the paper's framework (e.g., via lifting to the covering space and Dirichlet uniqueness), but it requires a contained, genuinely new argument replacing the failed Section 6 chain; the theorem itself survives.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: taken in  lexicographical order
\ell(w)=\sum_{i=1}^m w_i\cdot 3^{i-1}, &\qquad  w=(w_1, w_2, \dots, w_m)\in S^m.

issues.failure_explanation: The degree vector is enumerated lexicographically ($\gamma_4=\partial T_{11}$, $\gamma_5=\partial T_{12}$, $\gamma_7=\partial T_{21}$, ...), but $\ell(w)=\sum_i w_i 3^{i-1}$ is co-lexicographic: $\ell(12)=7$ while $\ell(21)=5$. Hence (re-deg) is not a rewrite of the degree vector but a permutation of its entries, and the jump conditions $f(v^k_{c_+(w)})=f(v^k_{c_-(w)})+\rho_{\ell(w)}$ (and the appendix shifts by $\rho_{\ell(ws)}$) attach to each cell $T_w$ the winding number belonging to a different cell whenever nonzero entries occur at level $\ge 2$. The constructed map then has a permuted degree vector (e.g., a prescribed winding around $T_{12}$ is realized around $T_{21}$) and does not satisfy the prescribed (homotopy-c).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redefine $\ell$ as the true lexicographic index (e.g., $\ell(w)=\sum_{i=1}^m (w_i-1)3^{m-i}+(3^m-1)/2$), or consistently restate the degree data in the $\ell$-ordering, in (re-deg), (eq:sg_gen_cuts), the spaces $H^k_m$, and the appendix.
issues.overall_effect: The Section 7 construction and the appendix prove thm.main only for degree vectors supported at levels $\le 1$ or symmetric under the $\ell$-permutation; for general higher-order degrees the constructed map has the wrong homotopy data.
issues.title: Higher-order construction indexes winding numbers with a non-lexicographic map $\ell$
issues.why_classification: A one-line redefinition of the index function restores the construction for all degrees; no substantive claim or method is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: H^k_m\doteq \{ f\in L(V_m^k, \R):\quad f(v_1^k)=k,\; f(v_2^k) = \delta_{1}+k,\; f(v_3^k)= \delta_2+\delta_1+k,\; f(z_+^k) = f(z_-^k)+\rho_0\}
it remains to check that $\mathbf{f}^\ast|_{\tilde V_m}$ satisfies the discrete Laplace equation at $z_{\pm}^k$.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof establishes the discrete Laplace equation at non-corner nodes and at the glued cut points $z^k_\pm$, but the values at the corner nodes $v^k_i$ are prescribed Dirichlet data on every sheet (def-H), and the Laplacian there need not vanish. For example, with $\rho_0=1,\delta_1=1,\delta_2=0$, the paper's own extension formula (Hext) gives $f_x=1/2$ and $f_{z_-}=1/10$ at level 1, so $\Delta(v^0_1)=(1/2-0)+(1/10-0)=3/5\ne0$. The quantifier '$\forall x\in\tilde V_m$' is therefore false as stated; the proof itself only addresses interior and cut nodes.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State (G-harmonic) for $x\in\tilde V_m\setminus\{v^k_i: i\in\{1,2,3\}, k\in\Z\}$, noting that the corners are the Dirichlet nodes of the covering-space problem.
issues.overall_effect: The theorem as stated overreaches; downstream uses (harmonicity of the projected HM on $G\setminus V_0$) concern only non-corner nodes and are unaffected.
issues.title: Covering-space harmonicity claimed at all nodes but fails at the sheet corners
issues.why_classification: A local weakening of the quantifier preserves the theorem's role and all downstream claims.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: where $c_\pm (v_i^{(m)})$ stand for the two itineraries of $v_i^{(m)}$ along the cycle ${\gamma}_i^{(m)}$, cf. \eqref{eq:sg_gen_cuts}.
Repeating the energy minimization along the lines of Lemma \ref{lem.minimizer} results in a unique harmonic function on $\Gamma_{m+1}^0$.
This can be harmonically extended as in Lemma \ref{lem.ext_harmonic_on_G} to a dense set of $\tilde{K}$

issues.failure_explanation: For a general p.c.f. set the proof never specifies how the cut vertex $\xi(\gamma_i^{(m)})$ is doubled: the two copies are distinguished only by the two cycle edges at $\xi$, and no rule assigns the other incident cells/edges (which need not split into exactly two 'sides' when three or more cells meet at $\xi$) to the two copies; different assignments give different covering spaces. Nor are the p.c.f. analogues of the key SG steps proven: refinement compatibility of the cut energy forms for the general energy (eq:energy_min_gen), existence/uniqueness of the cut-graph minimizer with multiple jump conditions, the modified extension formula at cuts (the SG proof used the explicit (Hext) and the 5/3 scaling), harmonicity at the glued cut points via the sheet-swap symmetry, and the extension by uniform continuity to $\tilde K$. Each is only asserted 'along the lines of' the SG lemmas, and the example recipe to 'select any vertex along the embedded image of $e$' does not by itself guarantee (pcf-cut).

failure_location.quote: The key constructions and the corresponding results in Sections~\ref{sec.cover}-\ref{sec.higherorderSG} translate to the present setting with minor modifications, so we highlight only the main distinctions from the previous proof for SG.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Specify the vertex doubling (e.g., restrict cut points to vertices where exactly two cells meet, adding this to assumptions (cycle_extend)-(pcf-cut)), and prove the p.c.f. versions of Lemmas lem.minimizer and lem.ext_harmonic_on_G (existence/uniqueness, refinement compatibility of the cut forms, harmonicity at glued cuts) for the general energy forms.
issues.overall_effect: The existence of HMs on general p.c.f. fractals (thm.pcf) is not established by the given argument; the covering-space construction for p.c.f. sets is incomplete as written, and the examples' claims that the assumptions hold inherit this gap.
issues.title: p.c.f. theorem asserted by unverified 'translation' of the SG proof; cut construction under-specified
issues.why_classification: The result is plausible and the repair follows the existing SG architecture with an added hypothesis and generalized lemmas — contained but substantial new argument, with at most a limited weakening of scope.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: There is a HM $f\colon K\to\mathbb{T}$ satisfying \eqref{eq:winding_vec_general} and \eqref{pcf-bc-hm}.
This prevented us from claiming uniqueness in Theorem~\ref{thm.pcf}, even though the gist of the matter remained the same as before.

issues.failure_explanation: The paper itself concedes that uniqueness cannot be claimed in thm.pcf (which asserts only existence), and no argument anywhere establishes uniqueness on p.c.f. sets: the p.c.f. proof is a sketch, and the uniqueness argument even for SG is not validly given (ISSUE-004). The Discussion nevertheless asserts that the constructed HM 'is still unique in a given homotopy class' by construction — an unsupported claim about what the paper establishes.

failure_location.quote: By construction, the HM obtained in the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm.pcf} is still unique in a given homotopy class, provided the latter is fully captured by \eqref{eq:winding_vec_general}, i.e., there are no nonzero winding numbers at smaller scales.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Weaken the Discussion claim to what is proved (existence of a HM with the prescribed winding data and boundary conditions), or supply an actual uniqueness proof.
issues.overall_effect: Readers are told a uniqueness guarantee for p.c.f. harmonic maps that the paper does not contain.
issues.title: Discussion asserts uniqueness of the p.c.f. harmonic map that is never proved
issues.why_classification: Deleting or weakening the unsupported sentence costs no formal content, since no theorem in the paper claims this uniqueness.
